statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and len(r) = len(queries). For every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), if i+1 < k then r[i] = -1; if i+1 >= k then r[i] is the k-th smallest element of the multiset {dist(queries[j]) | 0 <= j <= i}, counting equal distances with multiplicity. Equivalently, if the distances of queries[0], ..., queries[i] sorted nondecreasing are d_0 <= ... <= d_i with 0-based indexing, then r[i] = d_{k-1}.
preconditions: len(queries) >= 1 and len(queries) <= 200000; every queries[j] is a vector of length exactly 2; for every j and c in {0,1}, -1000000000 <= queries[j][c] <= 1000000000; all coordinate pairs (queries[j][0], queries[j][1]) for 0 <= j < len(queries) are distinct; 1 <= k <= 100000. For a two-element query q, write dist(q) = |q[0]| + |q[1]|, where |a| = a if a >= 0 and |a| = -a if a < 0.
